title: Brighton Stuns Arsenal with Historic 3-0 Victory
seoTitle: Brighton shocks Arsenal with 3-0 win in Premier League
subtitle: The 3‑0 win over the champions marks the club's anniversary and puts it among the league leaders.
excerpt: Brighton & Hove Albion grabbed the spotlight with a 3‑0 triumph over Premier League champions Arsenal on the club's 125th anniversary, climbing to third place.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Brighton & Hove Albion became the focus of world football after delivering an emphatic 3‑0 victory over Arsenal, the current Premier League champions. The surprising result, achieved on the day that marked the club's 125th anniversary, put the team at the centre of sports headlines and conversations.

Memorable win over the champions

Brighton demolished Arsenal 3‑0 in a standout performance that coincided with the club's 125th birthday. Fabian Hürzeler's vibrant side shattered Arsenal's hopes, who were aiming for an eighth consecutive win in all competitions – a feat not seen since 1903, when the club was still known as Woolwich Arsenal.

The match was a harsh blow for the Premier League champions, who had not conceded three goals in any competition since December 2023. Brighton, meanwhile, celebrated the occasion in style, turning the special‑edition shirts worn for the day into genuine collector’s items.

The goals that sealed the triumph

The goals came from Pascal Gross, the veteran interim captain, and youngster Charalampos Kostoulas in the first half. In the second half, new signing Chema Andrés sealed the win by scoring from a corner twelve minutes in. Brighton's attacking display was so dominant that the victory could have been even larger.

The new Premier League table

With the win, Brighton & Hove Albion rose to third place in the Premier League, just two points behind Arsenal, who now sit second. Fabian Hürzeler's side is showing consistency and ambition, cementing its place among the league’s top teams and defying expectations.

Offensive power despite absences

What makes Brighton's goal‑scoring feat even more impressive is that the team achieved it almost entirely without its main attacking unit due to injuries. Brighton now leads the division in scoring, with 16 goals in five games, overcoming adversity and demonstrating squad depth under Hürzeler.

Commemorative shirt controversy

To celebrate its 125th anniversary, Brighton players swapped their regular kits for a limited‑edition dark‑blue shirt inspired by the club’s first season in the Southern League Division Two in 1901. The move sparked controversy among fans, as the shirt was originally listed for £150 in a package that included an authenticity letter from owner Tony Bloom and a key‑ring. Those who paid for the unique item were pleased with the historic result on the pitch.

Sources: BBC, The Guardian, Arsenal.com.
